P-GLAD gas-lift system context (shallow injection, ~300 m). GAS bubble (low-purity CO2/N2 mixture), unlike every 1990s hydrate-era entry above, which are all liquid CO2. Reported consistently in two separate places within the 2002 thesis with no internal inconsistency (unlike Hirai 1996). Already partially checked in this project's Phase 1 literature work. Bubble is gas-lift-transported, not purely free-rising under buoyancy alone -- note as a secondary flow-regime caveat similar in kind to Hirai's forced-flow issue, though less severe. One of only two entries in this dataset that is a genuine gas bubble in (approximately) free rise -- see Cho & Choi below for the other -- and therefore one of only two directly valid tests of STUDY_PLAN.md section 3's gas-bubble rigid/mobile-sphere theory.

Primary paper read directly (MDPI JMSE 7(12):457). GAS micro-bubbles (30 micron), 4 bara, 160s retention time, no inline mixer. Far smaller bubble scale (microns, not cm) than every other row in this dataset -- expect a very different Reynolds-number regime. One of only two genuine gas-bubble entries in this dataset (with Saito 2000) -- useful precisely because it tests whether the theoretical framework holds across scales, not just within the deep-sea cm-bubble literature.
Same paper, second condition: 10 micron bubbles, 3 bara, 40s retention time, WITH inline mixer -- higher turbulence/mixing intensity than the row above.
